key_insight: Phase-coherent light at ω and 2ω can generate controllable spin photocurrents in centrosymmetric crystals, including channels with zero charge current.
engineering_relevance: Optical polarization and relative phase offer control knobs for light-driven spin transport, rather than a demonstrated AI or solar-cell efficiency advance.
method: Use coherent two-color driving to access an inversion-even third-order dc response.
Analyze magnetic and spin point-group symmetries to identify pure-spin channels.
Calculate responses in inversion-stacked bilayer 2H-MoS₂ and a centrosymmetric collinear altermagnet.
evidence_signal: Calculations in the two model systems show resonantly enhanced spin photocurrents whose magnitude and sign are tunable by relative optical phase.
watch_item: Experimental realization remains unproven in the abstract and requires phase-coherent two-color illumination with appropriate polarization.
paper_title: Two-Color Coherent Control of the Spin Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Crystals
